title: a-decision-is-a-question-bound-to-its-ticket-and-answered-in-the-inbox
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; codemother owns the care of the code; the question store is a record of truth in the commons (jurisdiction: questions/*.json) and the tool cairn/tools/question has users, not owners (Law 6).
ruling: none — by this ticket's own design. Akien's words of 2026-09-14 are the spec and ride from_idea verbatim; the decisions this build needs are the four open questions in `questions`, answered in the inbox.
decision_verbatim: what was the ruling should now be part of the ticketing or intention recording process. slash sorted should lead to questions, and if i can't answer then right then, for whatever reason, they become open questions in the iunbox. and yes, the answer to the question is the decision... ASSUMING THE ANSWER DOES NOT LEAD TO YET MORE QUESTIONS. If the answer does, we keep going around until you have all the answers you need. so lets make it look like that next.
pre_approval: none claimed — stands at his review queue; 'so lets make it look like that next' orders the build of the shape, and the four questions settle its choices.
intention: A decision Akien has to make is asked as a QUESTION bound to the ticket or intention that needs it — raised at /sorted (and /intent), answered in words, standing in his inbox as an open question until it is, and looping (an answer that bears more questions bears them as open questions on the same ticket) until the ticket carries every answer its build needs; the separate ruling packet, its store-forward, and its Stop-hook nag retire.
why: Law 1 (one intake for 'Akien decides X' instead of two — the ruling packet and the review queue — with the decision recorded once, beside the work that needed it, never re-derived); Law 5 (the decision shares the ticket's address instead of a parallel store the reader has to correlate back — the same finding that retired adjudications on 2026-08-28: 'the artifact IS the review surface'); Law 9 (what waits at his gate is what only his head can settle — a question is that gate's native shape, and the loop is how translation fidelity is reached); Law 4 (the loop's exit condition is a crossing gate, not a paragraph).
how: One tool, cairn/tools/question, the door for the existing open lane (CairnCommons/questions/open-*.json, ruled 2026-08-01 'edges become open questions'; the operator inbox already reads it — read_questions in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py, empty since 2026-08-27). Verbs: open (CC or a skill door raises a question against a ticket id — the record carries ticket, question, why_it_blocks, raised_by), answer (his words verbatim, answered_by from the caller's cgroup class, plus any follow-up questions the answer bears, each opened born_of the answered one), and list. The record is the decision: the ticket's `questions` field lists its question ids and the answers are read from the store, never copied. /sorted grows a `questions` packet field (the spec choices the caster cannot settle — today these hide inside builder_check and in chat) and the filing step opens each one. The emit chokepoint gains buildme_has_no_open_questions: TICKETME -> BUILDME refuses while any unresolved open question cites the ticket — 'until you have all the answers you need' as physics, not discipline. Then the retirement: `cairn ruling open` refuses with a pointer to `cairn question`, bin/cmd/ruling --hook leaves .claude/settings.json's Stop hooks, the /ruled skill retires, CLAUDE.md's ruling IOU and residue lines say so, the six skills that cite `cairn ruling open` cite the question door, the two build_inspector sieves that accept 'a ruling' as the same-act evidence (constraint_enforcement_holds, every_exemption_cites_a_ruling_or_an_impossibility) accept an answered question by id as well. CairnCommons/decisions/ stays as read-only record; nothing rewrites it.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) `cairn question open --ticket <id> "<q>"` writes open-<qid>.json through the artifact door and the operator inbox lists it under that ticket; (2) `cairn question answer <qid> "<words>" [--follow-up "<q>"...]` resolves it, journals the caller class, and each follow-up is a new open question born_of it; (3) a TICKETME ticket with one unresolved question is REFUSED at BUILDME by the emit chokepoint (buildme_has_no_open_questions) and crosses once answered — a proof a hollow build could not pass (revert the gate, the crossing goes through, the tooth reds); (4) `cairn ruling open` exits non-zero pointing at `cairn question`, `ruling --hook` is gone from the Stop hooks, zero skills tell CC to open a ruling; (5) constraint_enforcement_holds and every_exemption_cites_a_ruling_or_an_impossibility accept an answered question id as same-act evidence and still red a cite of neither. Horizon: one build. WRONG INTENT if a decision arrives that no ticket or intention can bind — then standalone decisions were a real class and decisions/ reopens as an intake.
traces_to: Law 1 (one intake for 'Akien decides X' instead of two — the ruling packet and the review queue — with the decision recorded once, beside the work that needed it, never re-derived); Law 5 (the decision shares the ticket's address instead of a parallel store the reader has to correlate back — the same finding that retired adjudications on 2026-08-28: 'the artifact IS the review surface'); Law 9 (what waits at his gate is what only his head can settle — a question is that gate's native shape, and the loop is how translation fidelity is reached); Law 4 (the loop's exit condition is a crossing gate, not a paragraph).

watchme.trigger: every BUILDME crossing attempt through the emit chokepoint, and every `cairn question answer` — the door pokes the probe after the act; no poller.
watchme.enough: 20 tickets have crossed to BUILDME after this gate exists with ZERO crossings recorded while an unresolved question cited the ticket, AND at least 5 questions answered with follow-ups (the loop went around at least once in the wild) — or ONE crossing that went through with an open question standing, which is the finding and the WRONG-INTENT clause.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: the crossings counted, the open-question count at each, the follow-up depth histogram, and every answer's caller class.
watchme.nexus: the what-Akien-decides tree — the same open lane the frontier projector (cairn/tools/edges) compiles; this probe is the first reader that measures the lane's THROUGHPUT rather than its contents.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and the counting learning block (5a4ec289bf15) once it reads who answers what.

gates_bound: code-seam gate-set: BUILDME rides the intent berth and the sorted berth (buildme_rides_the_intent, buildme_rides_the_sorted) — AND, once this ticket is built, rides its own new gate buildme_has_no_open_questions, which this ticket is the first to be measured by (its four questions must be answered before it crosses; if they are not, the gate it builds refuses the ticket that built it — the self-reference tooth). PROVEME: proofs sealed green with current fingerprint, hollow reading over every writes_to file, proof_coverage naming a tooth per falsifier clause. PROVED: verdict artifact against the falsifier. Feeds back to origin on failure.
children: none, because the seam is one tool with one gate and one retirement list, all in one build; the follow-on that is NOT this ticket is askscan's fate, held as question (4) rather than a child.
depends_on: 30531f6e1c5d (PROVED) — the question store is written through the artifact door.
owed_physics: a question opened by hand-editing open-*.json is refused by the artifact door already; what is NOT physics until built: nothing stops a crossing while a question stands (that is this ticket's gate).

cast_checks.assumption_check: Four load-bearing assumptions, each standing as a QUESTION FOR AKIEN rather than a settled fact — and by this ticket's own design they are opened as open-*.json in his inbox at filing, the first members of the lane: (1) the BUILDME crossing refuses while the ticket has an unresolved question (my read: yes, that is the loop's exit condition as physics); (2) CairnCommons/decisions/ stays read-only record and `cairn ruling open` refuses henceforth — no migration of the 50-odd rulings; (3) his answer may arrive as chat words recorded by CC (caller class cc, verbatim his), not only through `cairn question answer` from his own shell (caller class akien) — both accepted, the class journaled; (4) of the four Stop hooks (turnscan, ruling --hook, askscan, mailcheck) only ruling --hook retires here; askscan's signal is subsumed by the record but its removal is his call. Settled: the open lane's schema and reader exist (questions/_charter+why.json; inbox.read_questions), so no new store and no new inbox surface are built.

Also not wrapped: whether the answered question's text is COPIED into the ticket (readable at the address, Law 5) or READ from the store by id (one copy, Law 1) — my read is read-by-id with the inbox and `cairn operator show` rendering it beside the ticket; recorded in builder_check.

cast_checks.collision_check: Whys compared, none exclusive-and-terminal. (1) ruling 2026-09-10-exemption-reasons-are-not-rulings: its why is that the SAME ACT must carry Akien's authority for a drift; an answered question bound to the ticket carries it the same way — the sieve widens its accepted citation, the rule stands. (2) askscan (RULED 2026-08-14: build-time rulings feed back, never stop the work): the question door never stops work in flight either — it refuses the NEXT crossing, which the chokepoint already owns (2026-08-10 clearance-is-mandatory). (3) decisions/2026-08-01-edges-become-open-questions: this ticket is that lane's second tenant, not a rival — edges stay compiled from charters, decision-questions are direct-filed open-*.json, which the charter already allows ('direct-filed HOMELESS open questions'); the distinction recorded is that these are not homeless, they carry a ticket. (4) tickets 0fe1ccbfd33b/d9d08dd280ec (review replaces adjudication): same reasoning, adjacent act — review is his sign-off on the artifact, a question is his input INTO it; both live in the inbox.
cast_checks.builder_check: What a Haiku-level builder needs and the cast now carries: the store path and schema (CairnCommons/questions/open-<qid>.json; fields id, date, ticket, question, why_it_blocks, raised_by, born_of, resolved, answer, answered_by, answered_at, answered_verbatim_class); the write path (cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write, verbs open/answer); the reader to extend (inbox.read_questions groups by ticket); the gate's home (cairn/tools/base/transitions.py emit chokepoint, beside buildme_rides_the_sorted; red when any open-*.json with ticket==id and resolved falsy); the retirement sites (cairn/machines/ruling/cli.py open -> refusal text; .claude/settings.json Stop list; /home/akien/.claude/skills/ruled; CLAUDE.md lines naming `cairn ruling`; skills sail/chart/intent/tellmeabout/whatslefttodo/ruled; memory records-go-through-their-door.md); the two sieves at inspector.py:2416 and :2477. What the builder must NOT guess and is asked of Akien instead (the four questions in assumption_check). Left to the builder deliberately: the qid format (12-hex like tickets), the exact refusal wording, whether `cairn question list` is its own verb or the inbox suffices.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Looked. Smallest: keep the ruling machine and merely add a question field to /sorted — but that leaves two intakes for one act, which is the defect he named. Smaller than the cast: no new tool, /sorted writes open-*.json directly through the artifact door — but then /intent, the chokepoint and the inbox each re-derive the record's shape (three readers, no door; the exact shape the artifact door was built against). One small tool with three verbs is the floor.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: In-house: the open lane itself (decisions/2026-08-01-edges-become-open-questions; questions/_charter+why.json, schema {id, date, raised_by, question, whats_beyond, source, resolved}); the frontier projector cairn/tools/edges reads it; the operator inbox reads it; tickets 0fe1ccbfd33b and d9d08dd280ec retired adjudications for `cairn review` on the same reasoning (words, not a binary; the artifact is the surface); the ruling machine cairn/machines/ruling carries verify/conformers/fingerprint logic that the answer-in-ticket shape does not need (the conformer of an answered question is the ticket's own build, proved at PROVEME). Field: ADRs bind a decision to the change that needed it; 'RFC open questions' sections do the loop by hand.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: (a) That every decision has a ticket or intention to bind to — a decision with no work behind it (a Law restatement, a naming rule) has none; my read is that such a thing IS a ticket (the CLAUDE.md edit is its build), carried as a question for him. (b) That his answer arriving as chat words recorded by CC is acceptable evidence, as confirmation_verbatim was for rulings — the caller class will read cc, the verbatim is his. (c) That the 50-odd existing decisions need no migration: they stay citable by path. (d) That askscan's signal (a clarifying question asked after prebuild is a chain-intake gap) is subsumed, not lost: a question that becomes a record is countable by the chain without a transcript scan.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: None exclusive-and-terminal. Distinctions to record: (1) ruling 2026-09-10-exemption-reasons-are-not-rulings says an exemption cites a ruling — its why is 'the same act carries Akien's authority for the drift'; an answered question carries that identically, so the sieve widens, the rule stands. (2) askscan (RULED 2026-08-14: a build-time ruling feeds back but never stops the work) — the question door also never stops the work in flight; it stops the NEXT crossing, which is the chokepoint's job already. (3) memory records-go-through-their-door names `cairn ruling` as a door — it becomes `cairn question`; the memory line is updated in the build.
challenge_at_birth.back_up: proceed — his design words of 2026-09-14 are the spec; the cast carries four questions for him and they go into his inbox as the first members of the lane they describe.
